title: Continuing Student — Changes, Contacts & Requests
intro: For students already in the U.S. making changes mid-program (major changes, travel, internships, transfers). Most of these require action by your DSO — this checklist tells you what to line up. (Email-drafting and Gmail sending are on the roadmap.)

items.text: Talk to your academic advisor first to confirm the change and its effect on your program end date and full-time status.
Ask your DSO to update SEVIS and issue a new Form I-20 reflecting the change — request this before the change takes effect.
If your new major is STEM, note it may affect later STEM OPT eligibility — confirm the CIP code with your DSO.
Before international travel, request a valid travel signature on your Form I-20 from your DSO (signatures expire — check the date).
Carry a valid passport, unexpired F-1 visa, signed I-20, and proof of enrollment/funds when re-entering the U.S.
For an internship that's part of your curriculum, you need CPT authorization from your DSO on your I-20 BEFORE you start working.
Watch the rule that 12+ months of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility.
Get admitted to the new school, then coordinate a SEVIS transfer release date between your current and new DSO.
Complete transfer enrollment within required timeframes to keep your status; the new school issues a transfer-pending I-20.

sections.category: Getting the right contacts / drafting requests

items.text: Keep your DSO and academic advisor emails handy. Typical requests: a new I-20 after a change, a travel signature, or a CPT recommendation.
